newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher on spillover from CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher on spillover from CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher, boosted by spillover buying from CBOT soybeans although some pre-hedging was noted in late trade, floor sources said.
Elevators were reported to be pre-hedging in anticipation that the price runup would spark a pickup in country movement.
"We saw some pre-hedging on the close but the market held up pretty good," one floor trader said.
Speculations also continued to circulate that next week's Statistics Canada planting intentions report would show lower canola acreage than previously anticipated.
The July WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -10.42 Friday from -10.06 Thursday.
Flaxseed prices closed mostly higher with active trade in the May/July spread as positions were rolled forward ahead of May's first notice day next week.

Western barley futures ended mostly higher, supported by higher CBOT corn with additional support for new crop values linked to news CWB late Thursday raised its pool return outlooks for both feed and designated barley. July ended up $0.20 at $140.90.
Feed wheat also ended mostly higher with new crop boosted by news CWB had increased its wheat PROs.
Peas ended mostly steady with May unchanged at US$217.00. Oats were tradeless.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
